title: Opening of the Erie Canal
summary: The 363-mile Erie Canal opened in 1825 after eight years of construction. Governor DeWitt Clinton led the inaugural voyage aboard the Seneca Chief, ending in a symbolic Wedding of the Waters in which he emptied two casks of water into the Atlantic. The canal connected the Eastern Seaboard to the Great Lakes and the American West, and the National Park Service says population along its route quadrupled from 1830 to 1850 in Syracuse, Rochester and Buffalo.

uncertainty.note: Canal opened in 1825 after construction approved in 1817.

importance.justification: The canal linked the Great Lakes to the Atlantic Ocean, turning New York City into the continent's dominant port and transforming inland American commerce.

beats.caption: The Erie Canal opens as Governor DeWitt Clinton departs Buffalo aboard the Seneca Chief.
Connecting the Great Lakes to the Atlantic establishes New York City as the nation's leading commercial port.
